SAMPLE SIZE.evidence_source: Participants' mean semantic distance values were submitted to a 2 × 2 repeated measures ANOVA, with the two withinsubjects factors of cue type (cued, uncued) and constraint level (high, low) (see Fig. 1a). As was predicted, a main effect of cue type was found, F(1, 182) = 172.1, p < .001, partial η2 = .486. We also submitted participants' mean RTs to the same 2 × 2 (cue type × constraint level) repeated measures ANOVA (see Fig. 1b). A main effect of cue type was found, F(1, 174) = 239.7, p < .001, partial η 2 = .579. (Inferred N from F-statistic degrees of freedom: df_error = N - 1. For semantic distance, N-1=182, so N=183. For RT, N-1=174, so N=175.)

section_summary.extract_value: This section details a single experiment involving a 'Verb generation task' where participants' responses were scored for semantic distance and reaction time (RT). The study investigated the effects of cue type (cued, uncued) and constraint level (high, low) on these measures using 2x2 repeated measures ANOVAs. The findings indicated main effects for cue type on both semantic distance and RT, and a significant interaction effect for semantic distance, suggesting that noun constraint differentially affected verb responses based on cueing.
